max_tire.note: Restored trucks run period 6.00-16s; one 1959 on Bring a Trailer wore 265/75R16 all-terrains on its 16-in steel wheels. IH8MUD members warn that 15-in disc-brake wheels hit the FJ25's tie-rod ends, 15-in drum wheels won't clear the drum rivets, and most other 16-in wheels have too small a center bore.

tsbs.title: Toyota FJ Technical Service Bulletins 1959–1962
tsbs.summary: IH8MUD's FJ25 Owners Group hosts a converted PDF of Toyota's early FJ service bulletins covering FJ25s and the first FJ40s. A member describes it as including the first recall on the Land Cruiser. NHTSA's database lists no campaigns for 1958–60 Land Cruisers.

timeline.change: Toyota 'Jeep' BJ prototype with the 3.4 L B six; civilian series production from 1953
Renamed Land Cruiser in June because 'Jeep' was a Willys-Overland trademark; Toyota UK says the first export shipment went to Pakistan
20 Series launched (November per Toyota global, August per Toyota UK) on 2,285 and 2,430 mm wheelbases with B and F sixes
Range cut to the 3.9 L F engine alone in mid-year; exports reach Venezuela and Burma
Land Cruiser exports jump to 2,502 (Toyota); first dozen shipped to Australia in August
First Land Cruiser sold in the US, a single FJ25 through Rose Toyota
2,650 mm chassis added; Toyota do Brasil begins FJ25L production in May; owners report the 'Thunderbird' emblem on 1959s
Last J20s; the four-door FJ35V van is built for nine months; the 40 Series takes over in August
Brazil's 25-based Bandeirante switches to a Mercedes-Benz OM324 diesel; built until August 1968

identify.intro: FJ25s are rare and valuable enough that FJ40s get dressed up as them. IH8MUD's FJ25 Owners Group keeps a VIN registry, so check against it.

items.head: VIN plate format
items.body: Owners' plates read like 9FJ25-12645L or 0-FJ25-21848: a year digit, the model code, a serial number and an L suffix for left-hand drive. The plate also lists the engine number.

items.head: Frame and chassis tells
items.body: IH8MUD members point to the under-seat fuel tank, a flat floor with no hump for an offset transfer case, round rear wheel cut-outs, a centered rear differential, FJ25-specific rear spring hangers and an FJ25 steering center link.

items.head: Engine numbers
items.body: The registry shows F engines weren't fitted in strict numerical order, but the block number should fall in the right range for the frame. A 2F head or valve cover on an F-numbered block means parts have been mixed.

items.head: Year details
items.body: Owners report three-bolt front-fender mounting on 1958-and-earlier trucks (and some 1959s), the 'Thunderbird' emblem on 1959s, and a toolbox lid with diagonal ribs and five catches that changed around 1960, about when the cradle front engine mount was dropped.

values.intro: FJ25s trade as collector pieces. Originality, the correct F engine and restoration quality decide the price, and FJ40-based fakes trade at a discount.
values.note: Based on 5 Bring a Trailer sales from 2019 to 2026 ($14,001–$39,000), two 2026 sales of 1957 FJ25s at Mecum and Barrett-Jackson ($33,000 each, via CLASSIC.com) and RM Sotheby's $70,000 sale of a restored 1960 soft-top in 2019.

paragraphs: Toyota sold a small number of FJ25s new in the US: one in 1958, then 61 Land Cruisers in 1959 and 162 in 1960, by the IH8MUD registry's count. Most FJ25s sold in the US since then have come in from Latin America, often after restoration in Colombia or Costa Rica.

Every J20 is far past the 25-year mark, so NHTSA's exemption from federal safety standards applies, counted from the date of manufacture. State rules still vary on titling, VIN inspection and emissions. California is the hardest, so check before you buy, and make sure the import paperwork matches the frame number rather than a loose VIN plate.

production.intro: The J20 was built in small numbers in Japan from 1955 to 1960 and assembled under licence abroad. Brazil kept a 25-based truck in production until 1968.
